### bide audit verify-governance

```text
Usage of bide audit verify-governance:
  -checker string
    	path to the external verified oracle (astchecker); if set, it is run on the policy
  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never; -json is never colored
  -digest string
    	expected policy digest as hex (e.g. from a ProofBundle or the anchor); must match if set
  -json
    	print one JSON report on stdout instead of the text report
  -max-clock-skew duration
    	how far past this machine's clock a signed head's timestamp may be (default 5m0s)
  -max-input-bytes int
    	the largest input file, in bytes, the verb reads; a larger one is an error (default 268435456)
  -policy string
    	path to the serialized combinator policy (gsm PolicyBytes / WriteMachineAST output)
```

### bide audit verify-governed-action

```text
Usage of bide audit verify-governed-action:
  -action string
    	path to the action ProofBundle JSON (from prove -tool)
  -checker string
    	path to the external verified oracle (astchecker); if set, it certifies the policy converges
  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never; -json is never colored
  -json
    	print one JSON report on stdout instead of the text report
  -max-clock-skew duration
    	how far past this machine's clock a signed head's timestamp may be (default 5m0s)
  -max-input-bytes int
    	the largest input file, in bytes, the verb reads; a larger one is an error (default 268435456)
  -policy-bundle string
    	path to the policy-leaf ProofBundle JSON (from ProvePolicy)
  -pubkey string
    	public key as <scheme>:<hex> (ed25519, ecdsa-p256, ml-dsa-65, ed25519+ml-dsa-65) or bare ed25519 hex, or a path to a file containing it
```

### bide audit verify-quorum

```text
Usage of bide audit verify-quorum:
  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never; -json is never colored
  -commit string
    	path to the commit action ProofBundle JSON (optional)
  -json
    	print one JSON report on stdout instead of the text report
  -k int
    	the quorum threshold to assert: votes_for must be >= k
  -max-clock-skew duration
    	how far past this machine's clock a signed head's timestamp may be (default 5m0s)
  -max-input-bytes int
    	the largest input file, in bytes, the verb reads; a larger one is an error (default 268435456)
  -name string
    	the quorum's name, as passed to govern.Quorum
  -pubkey string
    	public key as <scheme>:<hex> (ed25519, ecdsa-p256, ml-dsa-65, ed25519+ml-dsa-65) or bare ed25519 hex, or a path to a file containing it
  -tally string
    	path to the quorum tally ProofBundle JSON (the quorum/<name>/tally step)
  -vote value
    	path to one vote ProofBundle JSON (a quorum/<name>/vote/<voter> step); repeat once per voter
```

### bide audit verify-receipts

```text
Usage of bide audit verify-receipts:
  -approver-keys string
    	JSON object of approver id to public key text (<scheme>:<hex>), e.g. {"ops":"ed25519:ab12..."}
  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never; -json is never colored
  -heads value
    	signed tree heads of the journal: a file with one head, or one head per line (the anchor log a published head is appended to); repeatable
  -identity-policy string
    	the certificate policy file (trust anchors, pinned intermediates, the approver-to-identity map; see docs/guides/hitl-approval.md): required for a certificate-bound receipt, which is checked against it and the log key instead of -approver-keys. The check is the identity at the time the decision became provable; revocation status is not checked
  -journal value
    	the run's journal export (audit.ExportJournal), one per run the receipts name; repeatable
  -json
    	print one JSON report on stdout instead of the text report
  -max-clock-skew duration
    	how far past this machine's clock a signed head's timestamp may be (default 5m0s)
  -max-input-bytes int
    	the largest input file, in bytes, the verb reads; a larger one is an error (default 268435456)
  -pubkey string
    	the log's public key as <scheme>:<hex> (ed25519, ecdsa-p256, ml-dsa-65, ed25519+ml-dsa-65) or bare ed25519 hex, or a path to a file containing it
  -receipt value
    	a decision receipt file, or a directory of *.receipt.json files; repeatable
  -update
    	write an anchoring proof into each receipt whose decision a signed head now commits to (an atomic rewrite of the receipt file, mode kept): from then on a signed head that omits the decision proves its deletion; without it the verdict is the approver's claim
```

### bide audit verify-run

```text
Usage of bide audit verify-run:
  -approved value
    	an approved policy digest; repeat once per allowed policy
  -approved-file string
    	path to a file of approved policy digests, one per line
  -cert string
    	path to the RunCertificate JSON (from audit.CertifyRun)
  -checker string
    	path to the external verified oracle (astchecker); if set, its verdict must agree with each policy's certificate
  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never; -json is never colored
  -json
    	print one JSON report on stdout instead of the text report
  -max-clock-skew duration
    	how far past this machine's clock a signed head's timestamp may be (default 5m0s)
  -max-input-bytes int
    	the largest input file, in bytes, the verb reads; a larger one is an error (default 268435456)
  -pubkey string
    	public key as <scheme>:<hex> (ed25519, ecdsa-p256, ml-dsa-65, ed25519+ml-dsa-65) or bare ed25519 hex, or a path to a file containing it
```

## bide version

Print the version and the artifact formats bide audit reads (-json for JSON).

```text
usage: bide version [-json] [-color auto|always|never]
  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never
  -json
    	print the version and the artifact formats as JSON

Exit status:
  0  success
  1  failure: an input cannot be read or the command failed; for check, an error was found
     (with -strict, any problem)
  2  usage error: a bad flag or argument; nothing was read
```
